chapter: Breakup of Hines band to Lefty Bates
title: Hewitt Abner and the Sutherland's McClean

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Was Hewett Abner (PHONETIC) connected with VeeJay then?
Yeah.
He's an interesting man.
You telling me.
That reminds me of Mack, the guy that used to manage the Sutherland, back -- I keep thinking of McConnell but it's not McConnell.
Oh, yeah.
Know who I mean?
Yeah, I know who you're talking about. He was manager -- first was a bartender.
Yeah, and he said he used to work out at the Grand Terrace as a bartender.
Yes, he did.
Like -- Horace Silver wrote this "Filthy McNasty" tune for him. McLean.
McClean. We used to call him the Twiglet, that was his nickname.
The what?
Twiglet.
Twiglet?
Uh-huh.
Where did that name come from?
I don't know how he got that name, unless he used to wiggle behind the bar.
I haven't seen him for a long time. He's a nice guy.
Yeah, that's when we was at the Southerland. With Lefty Bates.
You worked the Southerland with Lefty Bates? Yeah. How long were you with Lefty Bates?
